title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
abstract: arXiv:2610.35721v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Clinical trial prescreening requires distinguishing unmet conditions from insufficient evidence in patient records. Given patient records, criterion questions, and predefined answer options, we retrospectively compared JEV, a non-generative decision model returning native option probabilities, with schema-constrained Qwen Flash across 2,048 test patient-condition pairs from TrialGPT and question-answer datasets derived from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, all evaluated under strict Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policies to ensure clinical data privacy. Both models assessed conditions individually or in batches sharing the same patient context, with performance measured against reference labels. In batch mode, JEV and Qwen achieved similar macro-F1 scores on TrialGPT (0.652 vs. 0.660) and MIMIC-IV (0.807 vs. 0.814), whereas JEV substantially outperformed Qwen on MIMIC-III (0.768 vs. 0.534; $\Delta$ = +0.234, 95% CI: 0.187-0.281). translated_title: JEV能否支持临床试验标准的评估？
translated_abstract: 临床试验预筛需要区分患者病历中“未满足的条件”与“证据不足”的情况。在给定患者病历、标准问题及预定义答案选项的条件下，我们回顾性地将JEV（一种直接返回原生选项概率的非生成式决策模型）与模式约束的Qwen Flash进行了比较，测试数据涵盖来自TrialGPT的2,048个患者-条件测试对，以及从MIMIC-III和MIMIC-IV衍生的问答数据集，所有评估均在严格的零数据保留（ZDR）策略下进行，以确保临床数据的隐私。两种模型分别以单独评估或共享同一患者上下文的批量模式对标准进行评估，并以参考标签衡量性能。在批量模式下，JEV与Qwen在TrialGPT（0.652 vs. 0.660）和MIMIC-IV（0.807 vs. 0.814）上取得了相近的宏F1分数，而JEV在MIMIC-III上显著优于Qwen（0.768 vs. 0.534；Δ = +0.234，95% CI：0.187-0.281）。这一优势……
tldr: 本文提出非生成式决策模型JEV可在严格数据隐私保护下用于临床试验标准预筛，其性能与大型生成式模型Qwen Flash相当，并在MIMIC-III数据集上显著更优。
en_tdlr: JEV, a non-generative decision model, matches the performance of schema-constrained Qwen Flash for clinical trial criteria assessment under strict privacy constraints and substantially outperforms it on MIMIC-III.
